theorems.name: Kirkman.mem_renameSized
theorems.statement: For any point permutation e, a point x belongs to the relabeled k-subset b exactly when e inverse applied to x belongs to b.
assumptions: v,k are natural numbers; b is a k-element finite subset of Fin v; e is a permutation of Fin v.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.pair_subset_rename_iff
theorems.statement: A pair is a subset of a relabeled triple if and only if its inverse relabeling is a subset of the original triple.
assumptions: p has cardinality2; b has cardinality3; e is a point permutation.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.isSTS_image
theorems.statement: Relabeling the blocks of an STS by a point permutation preserves exact unique coverage of every unordered pair.
assumptions: IsSTS B, with genuine unordered three-element subsets of Fin v; e is a point permutation.
theorems.scope: PARTIAL: Preserves the STS property; no STS existence is asserted.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.parallel_image
theorems.statement: Relabeling a parallel class by a point permutation preserves its exact partition of Fin v.
assumptions: IsParallelClass P; e is a point permutation.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.resolution_image
theorems.statement: Relabeling a resolution preserves parallel classes, pairwise class disjointness and exact equality of the class union with the relabeled block set.
assumptions: R has (v-1)/2 classes and IsResolution B R; e is a point permutation.
theorems.scope: PARTIAL: Preserves an explicitly supplied genuine resolution.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.isKTS_image
theorems.statement: Relabeling a resolved Steiner triple system by a point permutation gives a resolved Steiner triple system.
assumptions: IsKTS B, meaning exact pair coverage and existence of a genuine resolution; e is a point permutation.
theorems.scope: PARTIAL: Transport theorem, not an existence theorem.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.development_sound
theorems.statement: A family consisting of invariant resolved fixed constituents and translated resolved orbit-transversal bases is an LKTS, including the correct number of constituents, pairwise block-disjointness, and equality of its union with all triples.
assumptions: Finite index types F,A,G; arbitrary point permutations act indexed by G; orbit labels key on all genuine triples.
card F + card A * card G = v-2.
Each fixed constituent and each free base is an IsKTS with genuine resolutions.
Every indexed permutation preserves membership in each fixed constituent.
Orbit labels are preserved by every indexed permutation.
Equal orbit labels imply that one indexed permutation carries the first triple to the second.
For each triple, equal images under two indexed permutations imply equality of their indices.
Orbit labels are injective within each free base.
Every orbit label has exactly one owner among the fixed constituents and free bases, where ownership is the actual image of its block set under key.
theorems.scope: PARTIAL: Conditional certificate soundness; covers the 17+2*19 order57 and 27+2*29 order87 patterns only when their missing seed packages and action facts are supplied. It does not assert either package exists.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.sts_pair_unique
theorems.statement: Two blocks of an STS containing the same genuine pair must be equal.
assumptions: IsSTS B; p has cardinality2; b,c have cardinality3 and belong to B; p is a subset of both.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.triple_has_pair
theorems.statement: Every genuine triple contains a genuine unordered two-element subset.
assumptions: b is an unordered three-element subset of Fin v.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.resolved_rows_sound
theorems.statement: If selected indexed triple rows cover each unordered pair in exactly one row and each (class,point) in exactly one row, then their image block set is an IsKTS. This derives absence of repeated selected block rows, point partitions, class disjointness and exact class union.
assumptions: An arbitrary finite indexed collection block : Fin n -> Triple v and a class index color for each row in Fin ((v-1)/2).
A selected finite subset of row indices.
For every genuine pair p there is exactly one selected row whose triple contains p.
For every class c and point x there is exactly one selected row with color c whose triple contains x.
theorems.scope: PARTIAL: Kernel-checked soundness of the concrete exact-one incidence convention used for pair covers followed by explicit resolutions. A pair cover alone does not meet the class-point hypothesis.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

theorems.name: Kirkman.lkts_fin
theorems.statement: Any LKTS indexed by a finite type can be reindexed by Fin (v-2).
assumptions: A family B indexed by finite type I and IsLKTS B, including its cardinality condition.
theorems.scope: PARTIAL: Supporting bridge to the exact Fin formulation of the book goal.
theorems.contribution: New formalization of standard finite incidence and orbit-development reasoning, specialized in its application to the existing released-constituent route; no new mathematical existence result or novelty claim.

negative_control: Two selected rows {0,1,2} and {0,1,3} on Fin 9 both contain the genuine pair {0,1}. NegativeControl.lean copies Formal.lean verbatim and attempts to prove the exact-one row condition for this concrete pair by ordinary kernel reduction. Lean must reject that false certificate column; this is the pair-column hypothesis of resolved_rows_sound, not unrelated arithmetic or a syntax error.
